candidate_data.description_en: Between August and November 2023 the Burkinabè military carried out three drone strikes with Turkish-made Bayraktar TB2 drones — on two crowded markets in Bouro and Boulkessi and on a funeral gathering in Bidi. Human Rights Watch documents at least 60 civilians killed and classifies the strikes as apparent war crimes because laser-guided munitions were used against clearly civilian targets. The junta under Ibrahim Traoré justified the strikes as counter-terror operations against Islamist fighters.

The African Digital Democracy Observatory documents the coordinated disinformation wave as an attempt to rally anti-Western sentiment and cover up the defeat.

The junta under Abdourahamane Tchiani did not publicly comment on the civilian casualties.

candidate_data.description_en: Since late April 2025, AI-generated videos and fake news have flooded sub-Saharan African social media glorifying Burkina Faso's junta leader Captain Ibrahim Traoré. The deepfakes show him alongside Beyoncé, Rihanna and Selena Gomez, claim $14 billion grain deals with India, or have him address the Pope in fluent English. One video gathered 626,000 likes on Facebook. Research by the African Digital Democracy Observatory, Full Fact and Dubawa traces the campaign infrastructure to Russia-linked networks; pan-Africanist influencers in Ghana, Kenya and Nigeria amplify the content.

Observers documented a broad social-media manipulation and disinformation wave aimed at stabilising the Déby succession — Chad ranks among the Sahel countries facing growing Russian influence and is part of the cluster of states targeted by Russian FIMI operations per Africa Center analysis.

candidate_data.description_en: After President Macky Sall postponed the presidential election on 3 February 2024, protests erupted. The Ministry of Communication, Telecommunications and Digital Economy suspended mobile internet on 5 February — while parliament was debating an extension of Sall's term. A second shutdown followed on 13 February amid civil-society protests. The ministry blamed 'subversive hate messages' on social media; the #KeepItOn coalition (Access Now), ARTICLE 19 and CIPESA criticised the shutdowns as a violation of digital rights and an instrument of electoral manipulation. Senegal had already restricted internet access and banned TikTok in 2023.

candidate_data.name_en: Burkina Faso: Junta blocks 13 international outlets, gives CSC power over social-media accounts with 5,000+ followers (2023-2024)
candidate_data.description_de: Seit dem Putsch im September 2022 verfolgt die Junta unter Ibrahim Traore eine zunehmend feindselige Medienpolitik. Suspendiert wurden u. a. RFI (Dezember 2022), France 24 (Maerz 2023), LCI (Juli 2023) und Jeune Afrique (September 2023). Nach Veroeffentlichung eines HRW-Berichts ueber ein mutmassliches Massaker der Armee sperrte die Junta innerhalb von 48 Stunden neun weitere internationale Nachrichtenseiten — Gesamtzahl: 13. Im November 2023 verabschiedete der Uebergangs-Legislator ein Gesetz, das dem Conseil superieur de la communication (CSC) die Befugnis gibt, Social-Media-Accounts ab 5.000 Followern zu pruefen, Medien zu schliessen, Geraete zu beschlagnahmen und Pressekarten zu entziehen — der Junta-Chef ernennt den CSC-Vorsitzenden selbst.
candidate_data.description_en: Since the September 2022 coup, Ibrahim Traoré's junta has pursued an increasingly hostile media policy. RFI (December 2022), France 24 (March 2023), LCI (July 2023) and Jeune Afrique (September 2023) have been suspended. After Human Rights Watch published a report on an alleged army massacre, the junta blocked nine more international news sites within 48 hours, bringing the total to 13. In November 2023, the transitional legislature passed a law giving the Conseil supérieur de la communication (CSC) the power to review social-media accounts with 5,000+ followers, shut media outlets, seize equipment and revoke press cards — the junta leader appoints the CSC's head himself.

It runs local offices in Ouagadougou and Bamako, sponsors Russian martial-arts tournaments, Wagner film screenings and a journalism school in Mali. Between 2022 and 2024 disinformation campaigns in Africa quadrupled — Russia-affiliated actors held roughly half of the social-media space on X and YouTube in Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger in 2024. A joint EEAS/VIGINUM/FCDO technical report (June 2025) documents the FIMI activities; Africa Corps inherited Wagner's information-warfare operations.

candidate_data.description_en: Whistleblower Ephrem Yalike-Ngonzo, in joint reporting by Forbidden Stories, PPLAAF, the Washington Post and Newsmax, exposes how the Russian disinformation system operates in the Central African Republic: with a budget of €7.3 million for January to October 2024, 'Africa Politology' ran targeted media campaigns in favour of the CAR army and Wagner, suppressed opposition voices and covered up Wagner mercenaries' abuses. Methods tested in CAR are now being replicated in around 30 Global South countries.

candidate_data.name_en: Gabon: Nationwide internet shutdown and suspension of France 24, RFI, TV5 Monde after disputed 26 August 2023 election, coup on 30 August
candidate_data.description_de: Am Abend der Wahl vom 26. August 2023 verhaengte die gabunische Hohe Kommunikationsbehoerde (HAC) eine Suspendierung von France 24, RFI und TV5 Monde wegen 'Propaganda und Desinformation'. Die Regierung verhaengte landesweite Ausgangssperre und schaltete das Internet ab — offiziell zur Verhinderung von 'Falschnachrichten' und Gewalt. Am 30. August stuerzten Militaers Praesident Ali Bongo, die Behauptung seines Wahlsiegs galt vielen Beobachter:innen als unglaubwuerdig. Das 56-jaehrige Bongo-Dynastie-Regime endete.
candidate_data.description_en: On the evening of the 26 August 2023 vote, Gabon's High Communication Authority (HAC) suspended France 24, RFI and TV5 Monde for 'propaganda and disinformation'. The government imposed a nationwide curfew and cut internet access — officially to prevent 'fake news' and violence. On 30 August the military deposed President Ali Bongo, whose claimed electoral victory many observers regarded as implausible. The 56-year Bongo dynasty ended.

candidate_data.name_de: Cote d'Ivoire: Biometrische Waehler:innen-Registrierung und Tablet-basierte Gesichtserkennung an Wahllokalen der Praesidentschaftswahl 2025
candidate_data.name_en: Côte d'Ivoire: Biometric voter registration and tablet-based facial recognition at polling stations for the 2025 presidential election
candidate_data.description_de: Die Unabhaengige Wahlkommission (CEI) der Cote d'Ivoire fuehrte Ende 2024 eine Waehler:innen-Registrierung durch, die rund 4,5 Millionen neue Waehler:innen mit biometrischen Daten (Fingerabdruecke) erfasste. Bei der Praesidentschaftswahl 2025 wurde in mindestens einem Wahllokal ein Tablet-System eingesetzt, bei dem Waehler:innen mit dem Finger eine Gesichtserkennung ausloesen. NGOs und das Africa Center weisen auf Risiken hinsichtlich Datenschutz und ID-Konsolidierung im Vorfeld der angespannten Praesidentschaftswahl mit dem Ouattara-Lager hin.
candidate_data.description_en: Côte d'Ivoire's Independent Electoral Commission (CEI) conducted a voter registration drive at the end of 2024, capturing biometric data (fingerprints) from roughly 4.5 million new voters. At the 2025 presidential election, at least one polling station used a tablet system in which voters place a finger on a tablet to trigger facial recognition. NGOs and the Africa Center flag privacy and ID-consolidation risks in the run-up to the contentious Ouattara-camp presidential election.

candidate_data.name_de: Cote d'Ivoire: Virale Social-Media-Falschmeldungen ueber angeblichen Putsch — pro-russische und panafrikanistische Netzwerke befeuern Desinformation (2024)
candidate_data.name_en: Côte d'Ivoire: Viral social-media false reports of an alleged coup — pro-Russian and pan-Africanist networks fuel disinformation (2024)
candidate_data.description_de: Das Digital Tech, AI & Information Disorder Analysis Centre (DAIDAC) dokumentiert eine Welle viraler Social-Media-Behauptungen ueber einen angeblichen Putsch in der Cote d'Ivoire, die sich als falsch erwies. Die Inhalte stammten ueberwiegend aus pan-afrikanistischen und pro-russischen Netzwerken, die Verbindungen zu den Junta-Regimen in Mali und Burkina Faso bewerben. Die Falschmeldung passt in das Muster der koordinierten russischen FIMI-Operationen in West- und Sahelafrika 2024.
candidate_data.description_en: The Digital Tech, AI & Information Disorder Analysis Centre (DAIDAC) documents a wave of viral social-media claims about an alleged coup in Côte d'Ivoire, which proved false. The content came predominantly from pan-Africanist and pro-Russian networks promoting links to the Mali and Burkina Faso juntas. The false report fits the pattern of coordinated Russian FIMI operations across West and Sahel Africa in 2024.

sources.title: Inside the Coup that Never Happened: How Social Media Fueled False Claims in Côte d'Ivoire
sources.publisher: DAIDAC / Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development

researcher_notes: Confidence medium — bisher nur eine starke DAIDAC-Analyse als Hauptquelle. Beim Promote nach Cross-Reporting suchen (FactCheckHub, AFP Fact Check). Klein gehalten als Severity 2, weil kein direkter Schaden, aber als Beleg fuer regionale Destabilisierungs-Disinfo wertvoll.
